hypotheses: Real Euclidean vectors of positive width d; epsilon > 0.
Nonnegative residual coefficient; positive integer layer count L for 1/sqrt(2L).
Embedding and each attention/FFN branch use parameter-free finite-epsilon RMS.
Scaling occurs AFTER output RMS; two residual additions per layer.

proven_properties.name: normalizer_lipschitz_reference
proven_properties.note: An existing, non-tight bound for one RMS operation; not a bound on the entire network or training dynamics.

proven_properties.note: The raw attention/FFN map can add its own sensitivity; this is not a whole-network bound.

implementation_mapping: The trace takes arbitrary raw branch vectors along the realized forward pass, allowing dependence on all causal tokens. First-position zeroing is represented by raw zero; guarded prefix selection chooses another branch/state with the same uniform bound. PyTorch-to-Lean correspondence is reviewed algebraically and supported by equation/caching tests, not proved by a compiler-verification theorem.
checks: Each new theorem with hypotheses has an explicit nonzero one-dimensional example using the actual FP32 epsilon. Source statements and proof dependencies were inspected.
limitations: The theorems concern real arithmetic, not roundoff/overflow in floating-point execution.
Embedding normalization acts on lookup activations; tied readout weight norms and logits remain unconstrained by these bounds alone.
No uniform bound on the full network Jacobian, optimizer dynamics, successful generalization, or epochs to 99% is claimed.
An RMS Lipschitz bound proportional to 1/sqrt(epsilon) can be large near zero; bounded activations do not imply small gradients.
empirical_decisions: The unchanged screen and full-suite selection rules still determine speed claims. Mathematical benefits and any measured regressions are reported separately.
